# 🚗 Spring Break Family Road Trip: Seattle → San Antonio → Austin → Houston

### Complete Trip Plan | April 10–18 | Family of 4

---

## 1. 🚗 Rental Car Recommendation

### Recommended Vehicle: **Mid-Size SUV** (e.g., Ford Escape, Toyota RAV4, or similar)

A mid-size SUV is the sweet spot for this trip. It gives you:
- Comfortable seating for 4 with legroom for the kids
- Enough trunk space for luggage without paying for a full-size SUV
- Better fuel economy than a minivan or large SUV (~28–32 MPG highway)
- Easy parking in city garages in San Antonio and Austin

**Avoid:** Compact cars (tight for 4 people + luggage on a 7-day trip) and full-size SUVs (unnecessary cost and poor fuel economy for this route).

---

### Estimated Rental Cost: **$480–$650 total**

| Detail | Info |
|--------|------|
| Pickup | SAT (San Antonio International Airport) |
| Drop-off | IAH (George Bush Intercontinental) or HOU (Hobby) — **see tip below** |
| Duration | 7–8 days |
| Daily rate (mid-size SUV) | ~$60–$85/day during Spring Break |
| One-way drop fee | Usually included or low (~$0–$50) on TX in-state routes |

> ⚠️ **Spring Break pricing note:** April 10–18 falls squarely in peak Spring Break season in Texas. Book your rental car **immediately** — prices and availability drop fast. Mid-April is one of the busiest rental periods in San Antonio and Austin.

---

### 💡 Rental Car Tips to Save Money

1. **Book through Costco Travel or Costco Auto Program** — consistently 20–40% below standard rates with no hidden fees, and they often waive one-way fees on in-state Texas routes
2. **Try AutoSlash.com** — free tool that monitors your reservation and automatically rebooks it if the price drops
3. **Skip the rental counter insurance** — check whether your personal auto insurance or credit card (Visa Signature, Chase Sapphire, etc.) covers rental cars. This alone can save $15–$25/day
4. **Avoid prepaid gas options** — you won't use a full tank every time; just fill up before returning
5. **Compare IAH vs. HOU drop-off** — HOU (Hobby) is closer to downtown Houston and typically cheaper to access; IAH is farther north but may have better availability. Since your flight is from HOU, **drop off at HOU**
6. **Book directly with Enterprise, Hertz, or National** after comparing on Kayak or Priceline — sometimes direct booking unlocks loyalty perks

---

## 2. 🏨 Hotels

---

### SAN ANTONIO — 3 Nights (April 10–13)

> **Target price point:** $120–$180/night for a family room or suite to stay on budget

---

#### Option 1: **Drury Plaza Hotel San Antonio Riverwalk** ⭐ *Top Pick for Families*
| | |
|---|---|
| **Location** | Directly on the Riverwalk — you can walk out the door and onto the river path |
| **Price** | ~$160–$200/night |
| **Room type** | Book a "two queen" room — plenty of space for 4 |

**Why it's great for families:**
- **Free hot breakfast included** — a massive money saver for a family of 4 ($40–$60/day value)
- Free evening snacks and drinks (5:30–7pm) — essentially a free dinner appetizer
- Rooftop pool kids will love
- Extremely friendly staff; very kid-oriented property
- Walking distance to everything on the Riverwalk

**Cons:**
- Slightly higher nightly rate than budget options
- Can be very busy during Spring Break — book early

---

#### Option 2: **Marriott Plaza San Antonio**
| | |
|---|---|
| **Location** | Adjacent to the Riverwalk and La Villita historic arts village |
| **Price** | ~$150–$180/night |
| **Room type** | Two queens available |

**Why it's great for families:**
- Large outdoor pool area — kids love it
- On-site restaurant so you don't have to go far after a long travel day
- Very walkable to Alamo, Riverwalk, and Market Square
- Reliable Marriott quality and consistency

**Cons:**
- Breakfast not included (add ~$15–$20/person if you eat there)
- Large convention-style hotel can feel impersonal

---

#### Option 3: **Holiday Inn San Antonio Riverwalk** *(Budget-Friendly Pick)*
| | |
|---|---|
| **Location** | Steps from the Riverwalk, near the Theater District |
| **Price** | ~$110–$145/night |
| **Room type** | Two queens or king + sofa bed |

**Why it's great for families:**
- Most affordable Riverwalk-area option that doesn't sacrifice location
- Kids under 18 stay free
- Pool on-site
- IHG points if you're a member

**Cons:**
- Rooms are more basic than Drury or Marriott
- Breakfast not included
- Can be noisy given its central location

> ✅ **Budget Recommendation:** Book the **Drury Plaza** if you can stretch to ~$175/night — the free breakfast alone saves your family $40–$60/day and actually makes it cost-competitive with cheaper hotels once food costs are factored in.

---

### AUSTIN — 4 Nights (April 13–17)

> **Target price point:** $130–$180/night | Preference: walkable to South Congress or downtown

---

#### Option 1: **South Congress Hotel** ⭐ *Top Pick for Vibe + Location*
| | |
|---|---|
| **Location** | Right on South Congress Avenue (SoCo) — the most fun street in Austin |
| **Price** | ~$175–$220/night |
| **Room type** | Two queen rooms available |

**Why it's great for families:**
- **Perfect walkability** — step out the door and you're on South Congress with food trucks, shops, and street performers
- Beautiful pool
- Excellent on-site restaurant (Café No Sé) for casual family meals
- The Austin experience in one block

**Cons:**
- On the higher end of budget
- South Congress can be loud at night (bring earplugs or request an interior room)
- Fills up extremely fast during Spring Break

---

#### Option 2: **Hyatt Place Austin Downtown**
| | |
|---|---|
| **Location** | Downtown Austin, walkable to 6th Street, Rainey Street, and the Capitol |
| **Price** | ~$140–$170/night |
| **Room type** | Two queen suites with separate sleeping areas — great for families |

**Why it's great for families:**
- Free breakfast included (major budget win)
- Suite-style rooms give kids their own space
- Centrally located — easy access to everything
- Hyatt points if you're a member

**Cons:**
- Less "Austin character" than South Congress Hotel
- Downtown can be congested — parking garage fees apply (~$20–$25/night)
- A bit farther walk to South Congress (about 1.5 miles or a quick rideshare)

---

#### Option 3: **Kimber Modern** *(Boutique Budget Pick)*
| | |
|---|---|
| **Location** | South Congress neighborhood |
| **Price** | ~$130–$155/night |
| **Room type** | Rooms vary — confirm two-queen availability |

**Why it's great for families:**
- Excellent price for SoCo location
- Quiet courtyard — more relaxed vibe
- Highly rated service

**Cons:**
- Small boutique property — limited amenities (no pool)
- Fewer rooms means it books out very fast
- Less consistent than a chain for family needs

> ✅ **Budget Recommendation:** **Hyatt Place Austin Downtown** gives you the best value with free breakfast, spacious rooms, and central location. If budget allows, upgrade to South Congress Hotel for a more memorable Austin experience.

---

## 3. 📅 Day-by-Day Itinerary

---

### SAN ANTONIO (April 10–13)

---

#### 🛬 April 10 — Arrival Day *(Afternoon arrival + tired kids)*

**Goal: Easy, low-energy, let the kids decompress**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 2:00–3:30pm | Land at SAT, collect bags, pick up rental car |
| 3:30–4:30pm | Drive to hotel (~15 min from airport), check in |
| 4:30–5:30pm | **Riverwalk stroll** — no agenda, just walk and take it in. Kids love watching the river taxis and the duck boats |
| 5:30–7:00pm | **Dinner on the Riverwalk** — try Casa Rio (iconic, right on the water, kid-friendly Tex-Mex) or Schilo's Delicatessen (family-owned, affordable, great for picky eaters) |
| 7:00–8:00pm | Gelato or dessert walk along the river, back to hotel |
| 8:00pm | Early bedtime — big days ahead |

> 💡 **Pro tip:** Don't try to cram in a major attraction on arrival day. A Riverwalk walk gives the kids something exciting to talk about without draining anyone.

---

#### 🌞 April 11 — Full Day | History + Adventure

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 7:30am | Hotel breakfast (Drury guests: free hot breakfast) |
| 9:00–10:30am | **The Alamo** — free admission, opens at 9am. Get there early before the Spring Break crowds hit. The boys will be at peak age for this — history becomes real here |
| 10:30am–12:00pm | **Alamo Plaza area** — walk through the surrounding grounds and the IMAX theater next door shows *Alamo: The Price of Freedom* (45 min, ~$10/person — optional but kids love it) |
| 12:00–1:00pm | Lunch at **The Arcade** or grab tacos from Mi Tierra Café in Market Square (5-min drive) |
| 1:30–5:00pm | **San Antonio Missions National Historical Park** — drive the 9-mile Mission Trail (Mission Concepción → Mission San José → Mission San Juan → Mission Espada). This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and completely free. Kids can get a Junior Ranger badge 🏅 |
| 5:00–6:00pm | Return to hotel, rest/pool time |
| 6:30–8:00pm | Dinner — **Biga on the Banks** for a nicer sit-down, or **The Friendly Spot** (outdoor beer garden with great food trucks — kids love the outdoor space) |

---

#### 🌞 April 12 — Full Day | Wildlife + Theme Park

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 8:00am | Breakfast |
| 9:00am–1:00pm | **San Antonio Zoo** — one of the top zoos in the country. Fantastic for ages 8–11. Budget ~$20–$25/person, opens at 9am. Get there early |
| 1:00–2:00pm | Picnic lunch near Brackenridge Park (adjacent to the zoo) or grab food at the zoo |
| 2:30–7:00pm | **Six Flags Fiesta Texas** OR **SeaWorld San Antonio** — pick one based on kids' preferences. Six Flags has better thrill rides (your 11-year-old will love it); SeaWorld has more animal encounters (better for the 8-year-old). Budget ~$50–$60/person if you buy tickets online in advance (significantly cheaper than gate prices) |
| 7:30pm | Easy dinner — pizza delivery to hotel or casual sit-down near hotel |
| Evening | Hotel pool if energy allows |

> 💡 **Money saver:** Check SeaWorld and Six Flags websites for Spring Break pricing. Both often offer "buy days, get days free" deals. Purchasing online can save $20–$30 per person.

---

#### 🌅 April 13 — Morning Before Checkout + Drive to Austin

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 7:30am | Breakfast (Drury: free; others: grab something quick) |
| 8:30–10:00am | **Pearl Brewery District** — a beautiful morning walk through one of SA's coolest neighborhoods. Saturday market (Pearl Farmers Market is Sat/Sun 9am–1pm — perfect timing!) Let the kids pick a pastry or snack |
| 10:00am | Return to hotel, checkout |
| 10:30am–12:00pm | **Drive to Austin** on I-35 (~1.5 hrs) |
| Optional stop | **New Braunfels** (30 min from SA) — quick stop at Gruene Historic District. The Guadalupe River area is beautiful in April and Gruene Hall (oldest dance hall in Texas) is worth a photo stop. 15–20 min detour |
| 12:00pm | Arrive Austin |

---

### AUSTIN (April 13–17)

---

#### 🎸 April 13 — Arrive Austin | First Evening on South Congress

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 12:00–1:00pm | Check in at hotel (or drop bags if early arrival) |
| 1:00–2:00pm | Lunch on **South Congress Avenue** — try Torchy's Tacos (Austin institution, kids love it) or Hopdoddy Burger Bar (excellent burgers, fun atmosphere) |
| 2:00–4:00pm | **South Congress stroll** — explore the funky shops, street art, and food trucks. Must-see: **Uncommon Objects** antique store (fascinating for curious 8 and 11-year-olds), **Big Top Candy Shop** (kids' paradise) |
| 4:00–6:00pm | **Barton Springs Pool** — if the weather is warm (April in Austin is often 70s–80s), this natural spring-fed pool is magical and only $5–$9/person. Kids absolutely love it |
| 6:30–8:00pm | Dinner at **Franklin Barbecue** (plan ahead — it's worth the wait) OR more accessible: **La Barbecue** or **Terry Black's BBQ** (no wait, equally excellent for families) |
| 8:00–9:00pm | Walk across the **Congress Avenue Bridge** at dusk to see the **bat colony** (1.5 million free-tailed bats emerge at sunset — one of Austin's most iconic experiences, totally free, kids are absolutely amazed) |

> 🦇 **Bat Bridge tip:** The bats typically emerge 15–30 minutes after sunset. In April, that's around 8:00–8:30pm. Arrive 30 minutes early to get a good spot on the bridge. This is completely free and unforgettable.

---

#### 🌞 April 14 — Full Day | Nature + Music

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 8:00am | Breakfast |
| 9:00am–12:00pm | **Barton Creek Greenbelt** — easy hike with swimming holes. Jacob's Well trail is approx. 2–3 miles roundtrip — perfect for an 8 and 11-year-old. Bring water shoes and a change of clothes |
| 12:00–1:30pm | Lunch at **South Lamar food trucks** or **The Picnic** food truck park |
| 2:00–4:30pm | **Blanton Museum of Art at UT Austin** (~$12/adult, kids under 12 free) — the main campus is also beautiful to walk around. See the famous **Ellsworth Kelly Austin** chapel nearby (free, stunning, kids think it's fascinating) |
| 4:30–6:00pm | Explore **UT Campus** — walk around the Tower, Littlefield Fountain. Kids love the college atmosphere |
| 6:30–8:00pm | Dinner at **Uchi** for a splurge (best sushi in Austin, kids who like sushi will remember this forever) OR **Torchy's Tacos** or **Valentina's Tex Mex BBQ** for a more budget-friendly option |
| 8:30–10:00pm | **Sixth Street** or **Rainey Street** — walk through Austin's live music scene. Even just walking the street and hearing music from open doors is the Austin experience. This is age-appropriate as long as you stay on the main strips and wrap up by 9:30–10pm |

---

#### 🌞 April 15 — Full Day | Texas State History + Outdoor Fun

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 8:30am | Breakfast |
| 9:30–11:30am | **Texas State Capitol** — free tours, architecturally stunning, kids earn a **Junior Historian** certificate. Your 11-year-old especially will appreciate the history after visiting the Alamo |
| 11:30am–1:00pm | Lunch at **Whole Foods Market flagship** (6th & Lamar) — sounds basic but this is the original, 80,000 sq ft store, like a food hall. Kids love the variety; it's an Austin experience |
| 1:30–4:30pm | **McKinney Falls State Park** — 15 min from downtown, stunning limestone waterfalls, swimming holes, and easy trails. Perfect April afternoon. Entry ~$7/person |
| 4:30–6:00pm | Return to hotel, downtime |
| 6:30–8:30pm | **South Congress dinner and shopping** — Amy's Ice Creams for dessert (Austin original) |
| Evening | Hotel pool or Barton Springs for a twilight swim |

---

#### 🌞 April 16 — Full Day | Theme Park Day or Discovery

**Option A: Schlitterbahn or Theme Park Day**
- **Schlitterbahn New Braunfels** (45 min south on I-35) — one of the top water parks in the world, perfect for April in Texas when temps hit 75–80°F. Budget ~$50–$60/person online
- Alternatively: **LEGOLAND Discovery Center Austin** (indoor, newer attraction — better for younger kids; your 11-year-old may find it too young)

**Option B: More Austin Exploration**
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 9:00–11:30am | **Natural Bridge Wildlife Ranch** (45 min, drive-through safari in New Braunfels area) — kids feed animals through the car window. Unforgettable |
| 12:00–1:30pm | Lunch in **Wimberley** (cute Hill Country town) |
| 2:00–5:00pm | **Wonder World Cave** (San Marcos, 45 min from Austin) — earthquake-formed cave, one of the most kid-friendly caves in Texas |
| 6:00pm | Return to Austin |
| 7:00–9:00pm | **Final Austin dinner** — somewhere special. Try **Odd Duck** (farm-to-table, amazing food) or a return to a family favorite from earlier in the trip |

---

#### 🏁 April 17 — Checkout + Drive to Houston

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 7:00am | Wake up, pack, breakfast |
| 8:30am | Hotel checkout |
| 8:30–9:30am | **Quick final Austin stop:** Grab kolaches from **Round Rock Donuts** or **Kerby Lane Cafe** for a classic Austin breakfast to go |
| 9:30am–12:00pm | **Drive Austin → Houston** (~2.5 hrs on I-10 E or TX-71/I-10) |
| Optional stop | **Columbus, TX** (1.5 hrs from Austin) — charming small town with historic downtown, quick leg stretch |
| 12:00pm | Arrive Houston |
| Afternoon | **Optional Houston activity:** Space Center Houston (~$30/adult, ~$25/kids) if you arrive with energy — it's outstanding for kids ages 8–11 and near IAH |
| Evening | Drop off rental car at HOU airport, hotel near airport if needed |

> 💡 **April 18 morning flight from HOU:** Book a hotel within 5 miles of Hobby Airport (HOU) on the night of April 17. Options: Hilton Garden Inn Houston Airport/Hobby, Hampton Inn by Hobby — budget $100–$130 for one night. This removes all morning stress.

## 4. 🌟 Top 5 Must-Do Activities by City

---

### SAN ANTONIO — Top 5 for Kids Ages 8–11

| # | Activity | Cost | Why Kids Love It |
|---|----------|------|-----------------|
| 1 | **The Alamo + Alamo Plaza** | Free | Living history, dramatic stories, the boys are at the perfect age to feel the weight of it |
| 2 | **San Antonio Zoo** | ~$20–25/person | One of America's best — carousel, Africa section, interactive exhibits |
| 3 | **Mission Trail (Junior Ranger)** | Free | Active exploration + earning a Junior Ranger badge makes it a mission they're invested in |
| 4 | **Six Flags Fiesta Texas** | ~$50–60/person online | World-class roller coasters; your 11-year-old will love Goliath and Iron Rattler |
| 5 | **Riverwalk Evening Walk + River Taxi** | Free ($5 for river taxi) | Magical atmosphere, great food, river taxis feel like an adventure |

---

### AUSTIN — Top 5 for Kids Ages 8–11

| # | Activity | Cost | Why Kids Love It |
|---|----------|------|-----------------|
| 1 | **Congress Avenue Bat Colony** | Free | 1.5 million bats is genuinely one of the most spectacular natural phenomena kids can witness — they'll talk about it for years |
| 2 | **Barton Springs Pool / Barton Creek Greenbelt** | $5–9/person | Swimming in natural spring water with cliff jumping spots — kids go wild |
| 3 | **Texas State Capitol (Free Tour)** | Free | Beautiful, historic, Junior Historian certificate — more engaging than you'd expect |
| 4 | **McKinney Falls State Park** | $7/person | Swimming in waterfalls 15 minutes from downtown — feels like a secret |
| 5 | **South Congress Avenue** | Free (shopping optional) | Big Top Candy Shop alone is worth the trip; the street art, food trucks, and quirky shops captivate kids |

## 5. 🛣️ Driving Routes

---

### Route 1: San Antonio (SAT) → Austin

**Recommended Route: I-35 North**

| Detail | Info |
|--------|------|
| Distance | ~80 miles |
| Drive time | 1.5–2 hours (allow 2 hrs during Spring Break) |
| Road quality | Excellent interstate highway |
| Traffic notes | I-35 through San Antonio and Austin can be congested — leave SA before 10am or after 1pm to avoid peak traffic |

**Optional Stop Worth Making:**
- **New Braunfels, TX** (30 min from SA, 1 hr from Austin)
  - Exit 189 off I-35
  - Grab breakfast/coffee at a local café
  - Walk through **Gruene Historic District** (15 min) — photogenic, beautiful, charming
  - If visiting on a weekend: **Gruene Hall** is open and atmospheric
  - Gas stations conveniently located at this exit

---

### Route 2: Austin → Houston (HOU/IAH)

**Recommended Route: TX-71 East → I-10 East**

| Detail | Info |
|--------|------|
| Distance | ~165 miles to HOU, ~190 miles to IAH |
| Drive time | 2.5–3 hours to HOU, 3–3.5 hours to IAH |
| Road quality | Excellent — well-maintained Texas highway |
| Recommendation | **Fly out of HOU (Hobby)** — it's closer to Austin via TX-71/I-10 and typically easier to navigate |

**Route Details:**
1. Take **TX-71 East** from Austin toward Bastrop (~45 min, beautiful Texas Hill Country transition)
2. Merge onto **I-10 East** in Columbus
3. Follow I-10 straight into Houston
4. For HOU (Hobby): take **TX-288 South** from downtown Houston (adds 20 min vs. IAH)
5. For IAH: stay on I-10 and take **I-610 North** then **I-45 North**

**Fuel Stops:**
| Location | Mile Marker | Notes |
|----------|-------------|-------|
| Bastrop, TX | ~30 mi from Austin | First good stop — charming small town |
| Columbus, TX | ~90 mi from Austin | Midpoint rest stop, several gas stations at I-10 junction |
| Katy, TX | ~150 mi from Austin | Last stop before Houston suburbs — fill up here before Houston traffic |

> ⚠️ **Houston traffic warning:** I-10 through Houston can be brutal, especially Friday afternoon. If driving on April 17 (Friday), leave Austin by **9am** to arrive before noon, or wait until after 7pm. The I-10/I-610 interchange is one of the most congested in the country.

### ⚠️ Budget Alert: You're $235 Over — Here's How to Fix It

The good news: you have several easy levers to pull to get under $3,000:

**Easy cuts to save $250–$400:**

| Cut | Savings |
|----|---------|
| Skip Six Flags — substitute Pearl Market + Brackenridge Park + free activities on April 12 | Save ~$200 |
| Choose Holiday Inn SA ($125/night) instead of Drury ($160/night) — note: you lose free breakfast which costs this back in food | Net save ~$30 |
| Choose Hyatt Place Austin ($150/night avg) and skip one paid activity | Save ~$80 |
| Pack a cooler with road snacks, lunches for driving days | Save ~$40 |
| Skip the Houston airport hotel — take an early-morning Uber to HOU instead of staying the night | Save ~$120 |

**Recommended path to stay under $3,000:** Skip Six Flags (replace with free/low-cost San Antonio activities) and bring a cooler for road snacks. You'll come in right around **$2,950–$3,000** while keeping all the best experiences.

## 7. 🧰 Practical Tips

---

### 📱 Best Apps for Road Trips with Kids

| App | Purpose | Why It's Great |
|-----|---------|---------------|
| **Roadtrippers Plus** | Route planning | Find attractions, restaurants, and stops along your specific route; worth the $30/year |
| **GasBuddy** | Cheapest gas nearby | Saves $5–$15 per fill-up on a road trip |
| **iNaturalist** | Nature identification | Kids photograph plants and animals; app identifies them — makes nature stops educational and exciting |
| **Geocaching** | Treasure hunting | Download before the trip — there are geocaches at almost every stop on this route. Your 8 and 11-year-olds will be obsessed |
| **Waze** | Navigation + traffic | Better than Google Maps for real-time Texas highway traffic alerts |
| **Spotify** | Road trip playlist | Download playlists offline before leaving; Texas has some dead zones |
| **National Park Service App** | Junior Ranger program | Track your kids' Junior Ranger badge progress across Alamo and Mission Trail |
| **Duolingo / Audiobooks** | Entertainment | 2.5-hr drives go faster with audiobooks; try *Hatchet* or *Percy Jackson* for ages 8–11 |

### 🎉 April-Specific Events & Festivals

---

#### SAN ANTONIO — April Events

**🌸 Fiesta San Antonio** — *Likely overlapping with your visit*
- San Antonio's largest annual festival — 11 days of parades, food, music, and cultural events
- **2025 dates:** Typically mid-to-late April (often April 10–20) — this may overlap directly with your April 10–13 stay
- Events include the **Battle of Flowers Parade**, **Fiesta Flambeau** (night parade), and over 100 events citywide
- Many events are free or low-cost; some require tickets ($15–$25)
- ⚠️ **Important:** Fiesta significantly increases hotel prices and crowds. If your dates overlap, book accommodations ASAP and verify your hotel reservation is confirmed (some hotels charge non-refundable deposits during Fiesta)
- ✅ **Upside:** If you hit Fiesta, it's an extraordinary cultural experience for kids — colorful, festive, food-forward, and uniquely San Antonio

> 🔍 **Action item:** Check [fiesta-sa.org](https://www.fiesta-sa.org) immediately to confirm 2025 dates and see which events fall on your April 10–13 window.

---

#### AUSTIN — April Events

**🎬 SXSW** — Note: SXSW runs in mid-March, so it will be over by your arrival. No concern.

**🌻 Austin Food & Wine Festival** — Typically late April (may be just after your visit, but check dates)

**🤠 Austin Rodeo (Star of Texas Fair & Rodeo)** — Usually runs through late March/early April. May have ended by April 13, but worth checking — rodeo events are amazing for kids.

**🎵 Live Music on 6th Street** — Not a festival, but a constant. Every Friday and Saturday night in April, 6th Street has live music in virtually every bar. Walk the street between 7–9pm with the kids and you'll hear 10 different bands in one walk.

**🌿 Eeyore's Birthday Party** — A beloved, quirky Austin tradition held in late April (sometimes April 26) in Pease Park. If the dates align with your April 13–17 window, this free community celebration is wonderfully weird and very Austin.

**🏃 Keep Austin Weird Fest** — Check current year dates; usually spring.

> 🔍 **Action item:** Check the Austin CVB events calendar at [austintexas.org](https://www.austintexas.org) for exact April 2025 event dates.
